about: The Senate, for the README's Limits: the seats, the rule, and why it is not modelled. Checked once on 12 November 2026 against the sources below; not computed by the pipeline.
elected_2026_source: Real Decreto 806/2026, art. 3.2: Ibiza and Formentera elect one senator each (Constitution, art. 69.3, as reformed in 2026; LOREG art. 165.2, as amended by Ley Orgánica 2/2026)
rule: LOREG art. 166: voters mark up to 3 of 4 candidates in a province, 2 of 3 in Gran Canaria, Mallorca and Tenerife, 2 of 2 in Ceuta and Melilla, 1 in the other islands; the candidates with the most votes are elected
rule_check: the 2023 count (BOE-A-2023-18907): in each of the 59 constituencies the candidates with the most votes are the ones proclaimed
party_line_check: outside the islands, every 2023 Senate candidate given their list's 2023 Congreso vote in the province, as a model driven by Congreso polls would have to: 7 of the 192 seats change hands
designated_note: Constitution, art. 69.5: each autonomous community designates one senator plus one per million inhabitants (LOREG art. 165.4: on the population in force at the election), so the number designated after 29 November may differ from 58.
